data.narrative:
Ultra Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jon Miller Schwartz, Max Friefeld, Chetan Parthiban, and Oliver Ortlieb. The company has raised $3M+ to date. The robotics and manufacturing sector comprises 10 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the narrow peer set for Seed-stage companies with similar characteristics remains limited.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach for this valuation. Using total capital raised of $3M as a proxy for Seed-stage value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $8M. The Peer-Median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient datapoints within the narrow robotics and manufacturing peer set at the same stage and valuation tier; applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M to $9M, with a median point of $8M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression anchor. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient same-stage comparables in the robotics sector, which limits external validation of the step-up multiplier, and reliance on total raised as a Seed-stage proxy rather than disclosed post-money valuations. Any refinement would require additional comparable transaction data or disclosure of the company's actual post-money valuation at the most recent financing round.
